content.text:
The structure is a central quaternary carbon bearing four CH2-NH groups. Each NH is acylated as NH-C(=O)-CH2-NH-C(=O)-CH(CH3)-N(ring), where the ring is a DOTA-like cyclen with three CH2COO- arms. Four Gd3+ ions are listed separately.

**Arm (one of four):**
C(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1

Check on the cyclen ring: N1, CC, N, CC, N, CC, N, CC closing back to N1. That is 4 nitrogens and 4 ethylene bridges, so a 12-membered ring. The ring nitrogen bearing the CH(CH3) group is N1 and the other three carry the acetates.

**Core:** C(CNC(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1...)(CN...)(CN...)(CN...)

**Full SMILES:** each arm is written as NC(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1, attached to the central carbon through a CH2.

The four Gd3+ ions are added as separate components. The image shows them with radical dots, but I wrote them as plain [Gd+3].

SMILES: C(CNC(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1)(CNC(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1)(CNC(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1)CNC(=O)CNC(=O)C(C)N1CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC1.[Gd+3].[Gd+3].[Gd+3].[Gd+3]
